Classification: Bloodline (pagan, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel}-adjacent)

Often mistaken for a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} subspecies, the Lhiannan (or Druids) are wild, fey creatures bound to a woodland spirit joined to the body of a vampire long ago by a shadowy figure called the Crone. As Christian forces stamp out or assimilate the old religions, the Lhiannan are pushed further from civilization, and their bloodline is slowly dying: the spirit that empowers them weakens and divides each time a Lhiannan sires a childe, so elders sire only rarely, hoarding what remains of the spirit's power. Lhiannan are fiercely territorial and strongly tied to forests, growing uncomfortable or ill in cities. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} bear them intense hatred for reasons elders only vaguely allude to as a "great betrayal."

Disciplines: Animalism, Ogham, Presence

Advantage: Lhiannan command Ogham, drawing on the power of nature spirits and the old wild places.

Disadvantage: Part nature-spirit themselves, the Lhiannan unsettle ordinary humans (who feel a vague discomfort in their presence) and read as distinctly inhuman to supernatural detection.

Organization: Scattered, isolated guardians of surviving pagan enclaves, with no central leadership; each jealously guards her own shard of the bloodline's founding spirit.

Suggested Viae: Beast; a few follow the Roads of Kings or Sin.
